  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.

      properties:
        type:

          format: uri

        title:
          title: Title

          example: NoResourceFoundException

        status:

          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true

## What I changed and why

The feature needed a persisted `registrationDate` that is (a) accepted optionally on `POST /api/owners`, (b) defaulted to the server's current date when omitted, and (c) returned as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` on `GET`.

**Behaviour (kept as small, cohesive edits):**
- `src/main/resources/openapi.yml` — added `registrationDate` (`format: date`, optional) to the `OwnerFields` schema. Because `Owner` is `allOf: [OwnerFields, …]`, this one addition gives both the request DTO and the response DTO a `LocalDate registrationDate` (Jackson serialises `LocalDate` as `YYYY-MM-DD`, matching the tests' `today()`).
- `mapper/OwnerMapper.java` — one `@Mapping` on `toOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)` defaulting the date to `LocalDate.now()` when the DTO value is null. This method is used **only** on the create path (`BuildOwner`); the update path (`ApplyOwner`) sets fields by hand and doesn't touch it, so an update never clobbers an existing date.
- `model/Owner.java` — the `registrationDate` field plus a getter/setter (JPA uses field access here, MapStruct uses the accessors).

**Persistence:**
- Added a `registration_date DATE` column to all four `schema.sql` files (hsqldb, h2, postgres, mysql) so the entity is consistent across profiles.
- Padded the positional seed `INSERT`s in `hsqldb/data.sql` and `mysql/data.sql` with `NULL` (the h2/postgres seeds use explicit column lists, so they needed no change).

I deliberately avoided adding logic to the already-complex `BuildOwner` step or introducing a new pipeline step + YAML wiring; the mapper default keeps the new behaviour as a single one-line mapping and touches no high-complexity method.

The test profile is `hsqldb`; I ran the full suite (`./mvnw -o test`) → **BUILD SUCCESS, 2/2 tests passing**.
